transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess it’s mostly that I’ve been having some trouble really taking in what people are saying. It’s not all the time, and I don’t mean to be rude or anything, but my wife will be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or rides, and I’m looking right at her like I’m listening… then a minute later I realize I didn’t actually catch half of it. I figured maybe I should talk to someone about it, if that makes sense.
Has this trouble focusing on conversations been something you've noticed since childhood, or is it a new change that started more recently?

I don’t think it’s completely new, no. I mean, I’ve gotten by okay, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was… but even back in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I’d be daydreaming or leaving homework in my desk. They’d have to remind me to finish classwork sometimes. So I guess there’s been some version of it for a long time, if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Aside from the trouble focusing, have you been feeling persistently worried, anxious, or on edge lately?

Not really, no… I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess, like anybody, but I wouldn’t say I’m persistently anxious or on edge. At least I haven’t noticed that being the main issue. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have off days like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down for days at a time or losing interest in things. At least nothing that stood out to me as a problem.
Right now, would you say this difficulty focusing is causing real problems for you both at work and at home, or is it mostly limited to one setting?

It’s… I’d say it’s showing up in more than one place, yeah. I’m not working a regular job right now, so it’s not “work” in the usual sense, but with the catering tasks I help with, I’ve had to double-check things or redo little parts so orders don’t get mixed up.

And at home, it’s caused some tension. My wife gets frustrated because she feels like she can’t always count on me with my cousin’s care. I don’t think it’s a disaster or anything, but it is causing real problems, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or find it hard to stay seated, or find yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively?

I don’t think so, not in any major way. I mean, I might shift around in my chair like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’m restless or unable to sit still. And I try not to interrupt people… I don’t think impulsive stuff is really the issue for me.

Is that what you mean, more like being physically wound up or blurting things out?
Do you often lose track of items you need, like keys or paperwork, or find it hard to organize tasks and keep appointments straight?

Yeah… I do, somewhat. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’m pretty often putting things down and then not remembering where they went.

Like my keys, my phone, catering receipts, even garden clippers — I’ll set them somewhere in the house and then spend ten minutes retracing my steps trying to find them. It’s embarrassing more than anything. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Thinking back to before you turned 12, did you also lose track of things like homework, toys, or supplies, or have trouble keeping tasks organized, similar to what you experience now?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s been a long time, so I don’t want to overstate it, but I do remember teachers telling my parents I was bright, just kind of… off in my own world a lot.

Before I was 12, I’d leave homework in my desk or forget to bring the right things home, and I needed reminders to finish classwork. It wasn’t like I was trying to be difficult. I just sort of lost track of what I was supposed to be doing. Is that the kind of childhood pattern you’re asking about?
Do you often find it hard to sustain attention on tasks like reading, paperwork, or long conversations, even when you're trying to focus?

Yes… I think that does happen. Not constantly, but enough that I notice it.

Like if I sit down to work out a catering order, or I’m listening through a parish planning call, I’ll start off okay and I’m really trying to pay attention. But after a while my mind kind of drifts, and then I realize I’ve missed part of it. I’ll have to go back over the same notes like I never really read them the first time.

It’s not that I don’t care about it. I do. I just… lose the thread sometimes. Is that what you mean?
